Trigger: Depleting one's own Willpower entirely (to zero temporary Willpower) while creating a Chimerstry illusion.

Since the Week of Nightmares, heavy reliance on Chimerstry has begun to corrode some @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos}' own grip on what is real. This derangement is a clan-specific hazard of the Discipline itself, rather than a product of ordinary terror, guilt, or trauma — the caster's own senses begin to blur the line between what she has made and what has always been there.

The first time a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.oWsHHlI3OS7cwvaF]{Ravnos} exhausts her Willpower completely while weaving an illusion, she suffers The Haunting (per Vampire: The Masquerade Revised, p.155, Dementation): she becomes plagued by the nagging, inescapable sense that something is wrong or watching, without any concrete cause she can point to.

With continued Chimerstry overuse under the same trigger condition, the derangement progresses beyond The Haunting into full-sensory hallucinations of escalating severity and danger — mistaking a friend for an enemy, perceiving a busy street as utterly empty, hearing voices that were never there, or failing to see a genuine threat standing in plain sight. As with other derangements, the character may spend a Willpower point (System) or a Willpower Trait (MET) to recognize the hallucination for what it is and negate its effects for the remainder of the scene, but the underlying condition remains until treated through extended therapy or similarly dramatic roleplaying resolution.

Also listed for Storytellers under Rules Reference (Storyteller Only): @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.rules-reference-st.JournalEntry.2d649361cb544a82]{Dissociative Perceptions Syndrome} (same write-up, kept there too for topical browsing).
